stem: A vehicle travels at 60 mph on a level road. Using a perception-reaction time of 2.5 s and a deceleration rate of 11.2 ft/s^{2}, what is the stopping sight distance?
eli5: Stopping takes two stretches of road: the distance you cover while you notice the problem and move your foot, then the distance you cover while braking.

stem: What is the minimum radius of a horizontal curve for a design speed of 50 mph, with a superelevation of 6% and a side friction factor of 0.14?
eli5: A car on a curve wants to keep going straight. Banking the road and tyre grip hold it in. The faster the design speed, the gentler the curve has to be.

stem: Traffic in a freeway lane has a density of 40 veh/mi and a space mean speed of 45 mph. What is the flow rate?
eli5: Flow is how many cars pass you each hour. It depends on how tightly packed the cars are and how fast the pack is moving.

stem: An intersection approach carries 1,200 vehicles in the peak hour. The busiest 15 minutes of that hour carries 375 vehicles. What is the peak hour factor?
eli5: Traffic within the busiest hour is not even. The peak hour factor compares the real hour with an hour in which every quarter is as busy as the worst one.

stem: A crest vertical curve connects a +3% grade to a -2% grade and is 500 ft long. How far from the start of the curve (PVC) is the high point?
eli5: Going over a hill, the road climbs less and less steeply, is flat for an instant at the top, then starts down. The top sits closer to the gentler side.
solution:
The slope changes evenly from +3% to -2% over 500 ft. It reaches zero after the fraction \frac{3}{3 + 2} of the length.

x = \frac{g_{1}L}{g_{1} - g_{2}} = \frac{3(500)}{3 - (-2)} = 300 ft.

stem: Which of these are regulatory signs under the MUTCD? Select the three that apply.

options.text: Curve sign on a yellow diamond

eli5: Regulatory signs give orders you can be ticketed for ignoring. Warning signs give a heads-up. Guide signs help you find your way.
solution:
STOP, YIELD and Speed Limit signs state traffic laws, so they are regulatory.

A curve sign on a yellow diamond is a warning sign. A street name sign is a guide sign.

verify.basis: MUTCD Part 2: Chapter 2B regulatory signs (STOP R1-1, YIELD R1-2, Speed Limit R2-1), Chapter 2C warning signs, Chapter 2D guide signs

stem: A flexible pavement has 4 in of asphalt (layer coefficient 0.44), 8 in of base (0.14) and 10 in of subbase (0.11). Drainage coefficients are 1.0. What is the structural number?
eli5: The structural number adds up the layers, giving more credit per inch to the stronger materials.

stem: Using the correlation M_{R} = 1,500 × CBR (psi), what is the resilient modulus of a subgrade with a CBR of 6?
eli5: CBR is a quick test of how firm the subgrade is. A simple multiplier turns it into the stiffness value that pavement design needs.

stem: A highway lane carries 500 equivalent single axle loads (ESALs) per day with no growth. How many ESALs does it carry over a 20-year design life?
eli5: Pavement wears out from the total number of heavy axle passes over its life, so add up every day for the whole design period.

stem: A signalized approach has two lanes, each with a saturation flow rate of 1,900 veh/h. The approach gets 40 s of effective green in a 100 s cycle. What is its capacity?
eli5: Cars can only leave the stop line while the light is green. Capacity is what the lanes could discharge nonstop, scaled by the share of time they get green.

stem: A road follows the Greenshields model with a free-flow speed of 60 mph and a jam density of 120 veh/mi. What is its capacity?
eli5: An empty road moves fast but carries few cars. A jammed road is full but nothing moves. The most cars get through halfway between.
solution:
Maximum flow occurs at half the free-flow speed and half the jam density.

q_{max} = \frac{v_{f}k_{j}}{4} = \frac{60(120)}{4} = 1,800 veh/h.

stem: A signal approach has a speed of 30 mph (44 ft/s) on level ground. Using a perception-reaction time of 1.0 s and a deceleration rate of 10 ft/s^{2}, what yellow change interval is needed?
eli5: The yellow has to last long enough for a driver who is too close to stop to keep going and reach the intersection.

stem: A subdivision has 250 single-family homes. The trip generation rate is 9.4 trips per dwelling unit per day. How many daily trips does it generate?
eli5: Trip generation is a head count of journeys. Multiply the number of homes by how many trips a typical home makes.

stem: An intersection has 12 crashes in one year. Its entering volume is 20,000 vehicles per day. What is the crash rate per million entering vehicles?
eli5: Busy intersections have more crashes simply because more cars pass through. A rate lets you compare a busy one fairly with a quiet one.
solution: Rate = \frac{crashes × 10^{6}}{ADT × 365} = \frac{12 × 10^{6}}{20,000(365)} = 1.64 crashes per million entering vehicles.

stem: A logit mode choice model gives a utility of -0.5 for auto and -1.5 for bus. What share of travellers choose the bus?
eli5: Each choice gets a score. People mostly pick the better score, but not everyone, and the model turns the scores into shares.

stem: A horizontal curve has a radius of 1,000 ft and a deflection angle of 30°. What is the length of the curve?
eli5: A curve is a slice of a circle. Its length is the radius times the angle it turns through, with the angle in radians.
solution: L = R × angle in radians = 1,000(30 × \frac{π}{180}) = 523.6 ft.

stem: For the same curve (radius 1,000 ft, deflection angle 30°), what is the tangent length from the PC to the PI?
eli5: The two straight roads would meet at a corner, the PI. The tangent length is how far back from that corner the curve begins.

stem: A crest vertical curve joins grades of +2% and -3%. The design requires a rate of vertical curvature K of 150. What minimum curve length is needed?
eli5: K is the length of curve needed for each 1% change in grade. A bigger change in grade needs a longer curve to keep the hilltop from hiding the road ahead.
